findings.issue: CTO 2 says the claim that orphan rows are unreachable must be asserted in a test. orphanRowsAreUnreachable seeds the orphan row with quantity 0 (stock.upsert(p, null, seller, deleted, w.id(), 0)), and reserving 1 from 0 is a shortfall whether or not the row can be reached. If lockForLine matched on seller instead of offer_id, or if the fallback used seller rows, the test would still pass. The unit test ReservationServiceStockRulesTest.staleOfferIdIsShortfall (line ~141) is also vacuous: it stubs lockForLine for a fresh random UUID that is never the queried OFFER, so it is the same as the plain no-rows case. In practice the code is correct (lockForLine filters on ws.offer_id = :o), but the condition's proof is missing.
findings.fix: Seed the orphan row with a positive quantity (e.g. 20), reserve 1 with a different offerId, assert OutOfStockException, and assert that the orphan row still holds 20 (stock.find(...).quantity() == 20). In the unit test, drop the dead stub or make it the real case.

findings.issue: CTO 5 and T6 ask for a concurrent write-vs-reserve test that shows no negative quantity. concurrentReservationsAreConsistent runs setStock once before the pool starts, then only concurrent reservations. No stock write races a reservation, yet the class javadoc says it covers 'write-vs-reserve concurrency'. The racy path is not exercised: upsert reads previous with a non-locking find, then INSERT ... ON CONFLICT, while reserve holds FOR UPDATE row locks and add() applies GREATEST(0, ...).
findings.fix: Add threads that call warehouseService.setStock(p, null, seller, offer, code, N) while others reserve. Assert that no row is ever below 0, that the final quantity equals the last absolute write minus reservations committed after it (or at least that it is >= 0 and the sum of reservation rows matches the successes), and that no deadlock or exception escapes. Otherwise correct the javadoc and get the CTO to waive the condition explicitly.

findings.issue: The 'Contract notes (TD-P9-04, TD-P9-05)' block sits in the middle of the product-service table, between the /api/seller/products/bulk/template.csv row and the /internal/offers/{id} row. The rows after the note (/internal/offers/{id}, /internal/products/{id}/sync-prices, ...) lose their header and no longer render as a table.
findings.fix: Move the notes below the end of the product-service table, as was done for the inventory note after /internal/inventory/variants.

findings.issue: Slice 1 review finding 5 is not resolved in the docs. Nothing documents the orphan-row caveats: (a) after a timed-out create, orphan seller rows stay listed in GET /api/seller/stock until a retry re-points them; (b) a late original write can land after the best-effort zeroing and leave N units on a discarded offer; (c) a concurrent retry can get 409 while the first request is still compensating. They are only in ADR 0004 in general terms ('can leave orphan seller rows').
findings.fix: Add one sentence on each case to the create note in endpoints.md and to the PR description, together with the deploy order.

findings.issue: Deviation review. The try/catch is harmless but mostly does not do what its comment says. publishAfterCommit can only throw IllegalStateException when no synchronization is active, which cannot happen under @Transactional writeStock. Kafka send failures are already swallowed in the publisher's afterCommit. The catch also wraps stock.offerTotal, a SQL query: on Postgres a failed statement aborts the transaction, so the stock.find on the next line fails anyway, after a misleading 'Could not queue stock event' warning. The deviation is acceptable, because a queue failure never fails a committed write.
findings.fix: Compute offerTotal outside the try (let a DB error fail the write as usual) and keep the try around publishAfterCommit only, or drop the try and rely on the publisher's existing send-failure handling.

findings.issue: Deviation review. Sending a null sellerId for an offer line with no owner is correct. Inventory resolves the owner through SellerDirectory and fails closed on 404, and the comment in OrderService:606 slightly misstates this ('fails closed' when it is really 'inventory resolves the owner'). Downstream, attach() maps a null item seller to PLATFORM_SELLER and re-tags the item, so the shipment and item are attributed to the platform even when the allocation (al.sellerId()) names the real seller. The behaviour is the same as before the change and only reachable when product-service omits sellerId.
findings.fix: Optional: in attach(), prefer al.sellerId() when item.getSellerId() is null and an allocation exists; adjust the OrderService comment.

findings.issue: reserveLines calls SellerDirectory.offer once per item, even when several items repeat the same offerId. The calls also run before ReservationService's idempotent replay check, so during a product-service outage an old order-service retrying an already reserved order gets 503 instead of the existing allocations. This only happens in the rolling-deploy window.
findings.fix: Optional: memoise the lookup per offerId within the request; accept the replay-503 as a rollout-only cost or note it.

summary: Slice 1 findings: all resolved except one. Mine 1 and security 1: zeroing is skipped for ValidationException, quantity<0 is rejected before offerService.create, and badRequestStays400 asserts a single putStock. Mine 2: syncPrices is outside the compensated block, with a test. Mine 3: the PUT offer 503 is documented. Mine 4: AC-9 now uses the real OfferService and reports 0. Mine 6: stockWrite helper. Mine 8 and security 2: OrderService sends sellerId null for an owner-less offer line, with an IT. Mine 9: imports. Still open is mine 5, the orphan and timeout-ordering caveats, which are not in endpoints.md. Security 3 and 4 are pre-existing backlog items. Slice 2 code is correct. The ReservationService fallback to platform rows runs only when the line owner equals Platform.SELLER_ID. A seller offer, or one with an unknown owner, with no rows gets the standard Shortfall(productId, wanted, 0), also under UNLIMITED, before any stock.add. Own rows that fall short are never topped up. Platform offers are still served. The owners map is keyed like merge(). InternalReservationController resolves a missing sellerId through SellerDirectory.offer before the @Transactional reserve: 404 gives null (non-platform), and any other error becomes UpstreamUnavailableException (503) with verifyNoInteractions(reservations) proving that no lock was taken (CTO 4). Seller writes publish one after-commit QUANTITY_CHANGED, only when quantity != previous, with qty = offerTotal (seller-only, offer_id IS NOT NULL, same variant_key predicate as find). Old publisher overloads pass nulls, and the publisher test checks both. Backward compatibility (CTO 3) is verified against the application's Jackson 2 mapper in both directions. The cart test uses the production KafkaJson deserializer (AC-4). Docs state the reserve sellerId, the 503s and the deploy order (product, order, inventory). The engineer's deviations (publish try/catch, null sellerId) are acceptable with the minor and nit notes above. The unit tests would fail if the platform fallback, the UNLIMITED exclusion, the unchanged-quantity guard, the 403 checks or the pre-transaction lookup broke. The changes requested are both for CTO-condition tests that cannot fail. The CTO 2 orphan test seeds quantity 0, so it passes whether or not orphan rows are reachable. The CTO 5 test has no concurrent stock write. No duplicated platform code was found: offerTotal has no existing equivalent, and SellerDirectory and the publisher are reused. Every AC is met; the verdict is request_changes only because of those two test gaps.
